intro: Kanker is a district town in the forested north of the Bastar region of Chhattisgarh, in central India. In the forest near Kanharpuri, beside a red-earth track, a reader found a tree that stands ruler-straight above everything around it, with plants growing on its bark high up, and sent us its photograph. We do not yet know its species, and we would like to.
meta_description: A very tall forest tree beside a track near Kanharpuri in Kanker district, Chhattisgarh, sent by a reader: where it stands and what we know.
question_meta: A very tall forest tree beside a track near Kanharpuri in Kanker district, Chhattisgarh, sent by a reader: where it stands and what we know.
question_answer: The Tall Tree on the Kanker Forest Track stands beside a forest track near Kanharpuri in Kanker district, Chhattisgarh. The reader reached it on foot; we have not confirmed who manages the forest.
question_context: A reader sent us this tree from the forests of Kanker district in Chhattisgarh, central India, with a GPS fix taken at its foot, and the photograph needs no words to explain why. It stands beside a red-earth track that runs off into the trees, and it is simply taller than everything else. The trunk goes up ruler-straight, without a single branch, for what looks like four or five times the height of the person standing at its foot with one hand on the bark. Only near the top does it open into a small crown, and on the way up clumps of leafy plants have taken hold on the bark, epiphytes that live on the tree without rooting in the soil. Morning light falls through the bamboo and the forest on either side. We do not know its species. The bark is dark and furrowed in long vertical lines; if you can name it, or know how tall it is, tell us here and we will add your words. If you go, stand where the reader did and follow the trunk all the way up.
